about: The Test Bench's seed list: every open vCGE test, by name and steps only. What raven575 records (results, notes, pictures) lives on the lab server, never here. Update this file (testbench/benches/vcge.json) with the work: add a test when a change lands, set status 'waiting' while it needs a build or a yes. Seeded 2026-11-14 from Team vCGE's open items.
title: The Test Bench
intro: Every open vCGE test in one list. Work down Needs raven575; Automatic reads the real CI runs by itself.

items.title: Redesign steps 1 to 3 on your phone and computer
items.why: Steps 1-3 of the easy + premium redesign are merged (wide layout, card-maker tabs with the mini card, Guess / Type it / Take it again). Tests pass in CI; nobody has tried them by hand yet.
items.where: The lab's Newest build (/vcge/latest/), once it shows build e1dbbfe or newer. The public site does not have steps 2 and 3 until the next Pages run.
steps: Open the newest lab build on a computer. Go through every screen with a sample card: nothing should need scrolling except long lists.
On the Card screen, try each card-maker tab (🎨 🖼 🔤 🧱 🔳). On the phone, the small card should stay in view while you change things.
Read a card with one hard-to-read line (shiny, small print or a smudge). Under the flagged line you should see Guess, Type it and Take it again.
Press each of the three buttons once and say what each did.
Do steps 1 to 4 on your phone too.

items.title: Redesign step 4: the green GO button
items.why: Step 4 is merged (PR #35, 20:41 UTC 11-14): green GO circle on Welcome, read without the OK press, one review page with Make it fancy / Just the contact. Not tried by hand yet.
items.where: The newest lab build (the public site gets it at the next Pages run).
steps: On Welcome, press the green GO circle and take a photo of a card.
It should read by itself, without pressing OK, and land on one review page.
Press 🎨 Make it fancy: you should land in the card maker.
Go back, press ⚡ Just the contact: you should land on Share.
Check Step by step still works the old way.

interactive.thread: 🐢 Make vCGE easy and premium on every screen
interactive.how: After each step, post what the screen shows (a screenshot is best) so Shutout can check the flow before step 5 starts.

items.title: Redesign steps 5 to 7: icons, colour-vision tint, Easy touch
items.why: Not built yet. Listed so you can see they are coming; each gets its own steps when it lands.
steps: Step 5: every button icon reads clearly at phone size.
Step 6: with the colour-vision setting on, the art changes colour but your photo and the card's own colours stay true.
Step 7: with Easy touch on, buttons are bigger and wipe takes two taps instead of a hold.

items.title: QR styles: find them, pick one, scan it
items.why: The high-contrast QR styles are merged and live, but on 11-12 you could not find them. A choice card on where they should also show (Card screen) is still open in the QR thread.
items.where: The public site (https://real-raven575.github.io/vCGE-Master/) or the newest lab build.
steps: Make a contact, go to Share and open Save QR image.
Try three different colour pairs and two dot shapes.
Scan each saved QR with your phone's own camera app: does it open the contact?
Say whether this is where you expect the styles to be, or whether they belong on the Card screen too.

interactive.how: Your answer to step 4 settles the open choice card there.

decision.ask: Should the QR styles also show on the Card screen?
decision.where: the choice card in the thread "🦓 Add high-contrast QR styles"
decision.label: Open Claude, then that thread

items.title: PDF export shows the QR code
items.why: The blank-QR-in-PDF fix and the print follow-up (QR style and size on the sheet) are merged and on the public site since Pages run #5. Not tried by hand.
items.where: The public site, on a computer and on your phone.
steps: Make a contact, go to Share and export or print it as PDF.
Open the PDF: is the QR code there (not a blank square)?
Scan the QR in the PDF with your phone: does it open the contact?
Try the 5 cm size and a styled QR: does the PDF still show it?

items.title: Accuracy round 1: printed QR and phone numbers
items.why: Merged and live: the app reads a QR printed on a card, and re-reads phone numbers digits-only (it used to turn 555 into 55).
steps: Snap a card that has a QR code printed on it. Do the fields from the QR show up?
Snap a card whose phone number has repeated digits (like 555 or 1100). Is every digit right?
Press Cancel while it is still looking for the QR: does it stop cleanly?

items.title: Smart burst camera through its paces
items.why: Live since 11-13 and you said it works. Its beta feedback (dim light, glare, the light button) is still to come.
items.where: The public site on your phone.
steps: Snap a card in dim light. Is the result sharp?
Snap a shiny card under a lamp. Does the glare go down, or do you get the advice to retake with the light?
If your phone has a flashlight, is the light button there? Does it stay on after Retake?
Snap five cards quickly in a row. Any freeze or a wrong card?

items.title: App test builds: Android, Windows, Linux
items.why: The app wrappers are merged; test builds from main b128dc4 were posted 11-13 and expire around 11-27. Android export and download are untested. First Android findings (2026-11-14) are split out below.
items.where: GitHub Actions artifacts of run 43365848599 (android, windows, linux). The builds are unsigned, so Windows and Android warn first.
steps: Android: install the APK, open the app, allow the camera, snap a card.
Android: export the contact. Did it land in Contacts or Downloads?
Windows: install, open, snap or upload a card, export.
Linux: install the .deb or AppImage, open, upload a card, export.
On each: the app must work with Wi-Fi off.

interactive.how: Post what each install and export step shows, so the Android export path can be fixed step by step if it fails.

items.title: Android app: the top of the app sits under the phone's status bar
items.why: Found by raven575 on 2026-11-14 in the Android test build: the app's top row goes up into the phone's status bar, so buttons there are hidden or hard to press. Needs a fix (safe-area space at the top), then this retest.
items.where: The next Android test build after the fix.
steps: Open the app on the Android phone.
Is anything at the top hidden behind the clock, battery or notch? Can you press every top button easily?
Turn the phone sideways and check again.
Do the same on the Card and Share screens.

interactive.how: Post a screenshot of the top of each screen so the fix can be checked before the next build.

items.title: Android app: Export as contact really saves to Contacts
items.why: Found by raven575 on 2026-11-14: Export as contact looked like it saved, but the made-up test contact (Lena) was not found in the phone's Contacts. Not fixed yet; the cause is not known.
items.where: The Android test build. Use only made-up sample contacts.
steps: Make a contact from a pilot sample or a made-up card and note its name.
Press Export as contact. Write down exactly what the phone shows (a share sheet, a file saved, a Contacts screen, or nothing).
Open the phone's Contacts and search for that name.
If it is not there, open Files > Downloads: is there a .vcf file? Tap it: does Contacts offer to import it?

interactive.how: Post what the phone shows after each step (a screenshot is best) so Airlock can follow the export path step by step.

items.title: Android app: pilot sample contacts are missing
items.why: Found by raven575 on 2026-11-14: the pilots' sample information was not in the Android build. It may be a different build (the plain edition has no pilot samples by design) or a bug; to check.
items.where: The Android test build; compare with the public site.
steps: On the Android app, open the sample contacts. Which names show (pilots, or 'Sample contact' people)?
Open the About or Settings screen and note the version and build shown.
Do the same on the public site and say what differs.

interactive.how: Post the version line and a screenshot of the samples list so the build can be identified.

items.title: Public site: newest build and the right version label
items.why: The public site runs main bb3c05d (Pages run #5) but still says 0.8.1, and redesign steps 2 and 3 are not on it. Pages only deploys when you press Run.
items.where: GitHub > vCGE-Master > Actions > Pages > Run workflow (branch main).
steps: Run the Pages workflow on main.
Open the public site and note the version it shows.
Check the Card screen has the card-maker tabs (that proves step 2 is there).

decision.ask: Run the Pages deploy on main?
decision.label: Open the Pages Run button

items.title: The Scriptorium: mark what the 54 samples really say
items.why: The handwriting bench is live with 54 samples; until you mark them, the handwriting score is only a guess.
steps: Open the Scriptorium and go through the samples, fixing any line that is wrong.
Mark any sample you cannot read as unreadable.
Add a few real handwriting photos with the upload button (no real names or numbers).

items.title: Card Inbox: the first real card
items.why: The Card Inbox is live but has never had a real card. Its photo-against-video numbers decide whether the app reads a burst of video frames.
steps: Give the card a nickname (never a real name) and drop 5 to 10 photos of it from different angles.
Drop a 3 to 5 second clip of the same card.
Press Run new angles, then fill in the right answers once and save.
Read the summary: photos, video frames, all angles voted.

items.title: Camera retests on Android: pinch zoom and upload
items.why: Two older camera fixes were never retested on a real phone: the fast pinch on the crop screen, and the upload button showing the camera-in-use notice.
items.where: The public site on your Android phone in Chrome.
steps: Take a photo, then on the crop screen pinch quickly in and out. Does the zoom follow your fingers?
Zoom to a corner of the card: can any corner reach the centre?
Press Upload and wait in the picker for a few seconds: no camera-in-use message should appear behind it.

interactive.how: If a step fails, post a screen recording or screenshot of that step before going on.

items.title: Later: passkey sign-in for page-level approvals
items.why: You asked (21:05 UTC 11-14) to list this for later: answer yes/no choices right on this page, signed in with a passkey, instead of opening Claude. Not started; until then each choice links to claude.ai.
steps: Say when to start it, and it gets its own thread and real steps.

items.why: Every push to main runs unit tests, 7 browsers and phones, 3 desktop builds and the Android emulator.
